3: description: Up-to-date Microsoft Graph API knowledge for AI agents. Search 27,700+ Graph APIs, endpoint docs, resource schemas, and community samples — all locally, no network calls. Use when the agent needs to find, understand, or call Microsoft Graph endpoints.

10: # Microsoft Graph Agent Skill
11: 
12: Search, look up, and call any of the 27,700+ Microsoft Graph APIs — all locally, no network calls needed. Use the three search commands to find the right endpoint, check permissions and parameters, then optionally execute calls directly or hand off to a Graph MCP server.
13: 
14: ## What's Included
15: 
16: The Microsoft Graph API has **27,700+ endpoints** updated weekly — well past LLM training cutoffs. This skill bundles the complete API surface as local indexes that you search instantly with no network calls.
17: 
18: | Index | Count | What it contains |
19: |---|---|---|
20: | OpenAPI endpoints | 27,700+ | Path, method, summary, description, permission scopes |
21: | Endpoint docs | 6,200+ | Permissions (delegated/app), query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties |
22: | Resource schemas | 4,200+ | All properties with types, supported `$filter` operators, default/select-only flags |
23: | Community samples | Growing | Hand-verified queries mapping natural-language tasks to exact API calls |
24: 
25: ## How to Run
26: 
27: The `msgraph` CLI is bundled with this skill. Run all commands through the launcher script in this skill's directory:
28: 
29: - **macOS / Linux**: `bash <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.sh <command> [args...]`
30: - **Windows**: `powershell <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.ps1 <command> [args...]`
31: 
32: For example, to search for mail-related APIs on macOS:
33: 
34: ```
35: bash /home/user/.opencode/skills/msgraph/scripts/run.sh openapi-search --query "send mail"
36: ```
37: 
38: In all examples below, `msgraph` is shorthand for the full launcher invocation.
39: 
40: ## Finding the Right API
41: 
42: This is the primary purpose of the skill. Follow this progressive lookup strategy — each level adds detail:
43: 
44: 1. **Your own knowledge** — try first for well-known endpoints (`/me`, `/users`, `/groups`).
45: 2. **`sample-search`** — curated, hand-verified samples. Highest quality. Use for common tasks and multi-step workflows.
46: 3. **`api-docs-search`** — per-endpoint permissions, supported query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties, and resource property details with filter operators.
47: 4. **`openapi-search`** — full catalog of 27,700 Graph APIs. Use when you cannot find the endpoint any other way.
48: 5. **Reference files** — concept docs on query parameters, advanced queries, paging, batching, throttling, errors, and best practices. Read only when you need specific guidance.
49: 
50: This order is guidance — adapt based on the task. For example, jump straight to `api-docs-search` if you already know the endpoint but need its permissions.
51: 
52: ### sample-search
53: 
54: Search curated community samples that map natural-language tasks to exact Microsoft Graph API queries:
55: 
56: ```
57: msgraph sample-search --query "conditional access policies"
58: msgraph sample-search --product entra
59: msgraph sample-search --query "managed devices" --product intune
60: ```
61: 
62: | Flag | Description |
63: |---|---|
64: | `--query` | Free-text search (searches intent and query fields) |
65: | `--product` | Filter by product: `entra`, `intune`, `exchange`, `teams`, `sharepoint`, `security`, `general` |
66: | `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |
67: 
68: At least one of `--query` or `--product` is required. Results include multi-step workflows.
69: 
70: ### api-docs-search
71: 
72: Look up detailed documentation for a specific endpoint or resource type:
73: 
74: ```
75: msgraph api-docs-search --endpoint /users --method GET
76: msgraph api-docs-search --resource user
77: msgraph api-docs-search --query "ConsistencyLevel"
78: ```
79: 
80: | Flag | Description |
81: |---|---|
82: | `--endpoint` | Search by endpoint path (e.g. `/users`, `/me/messages`) |
83: | `--resource` | Search by resource type name (e.g. `user`, `group`, `message`) |
84: | `--method` | Filter by HTTP method: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` |
85: | `--query` | Free-text search across all fields |
86: | `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |
87: 
88: At least one of `--endpoint`, `--resource`, or `--query` is required.
89: 
90: **Endpoint results** include: required permissions (delegated work/school, delegated personal, application), supported OData query parameters, required headers, default properties, and endpoint-specific notes.
91: 
92: **Resource results** include: all properties with types, supported `$filter` operators (eq, ne, startsWith, etc.), and whether each property is returned by default or requires `$select`.
93: 
94: ### openapi-search
95: 
96: Search the full OpenAPI catalog of 27,700 Microsoft Graph APIs:
97: 
98: ```
99: msgraph openapi-search --query "send mail"
100: msgraph openapi-search --resource messages --method GET
101: ```
102: 
103: | Flag | Description |
104: |---|---|
105: | `--query` | Free-text search (searches path, summary, description) |
106: | `--resource` | Filter by resource name (e.g. `users`, `groups`, `messages`) |
107: | `--method` | Filter by HTTP method |
108: | `--limit` | Max results (default 20) |
109: 
110: At least one of `--query`, `--resource`, or `--method` is required.
111: 
112: ## Using with MCP Servers
113: 
114: If the agent has access to a Microsoft Graph MCP server (such as [lokka.dev](https://lokka.dev) or any other Microsoft Graph MCP server), use the search tools above to find the right endpoint, permissions, and request syntax, then use the information with the MCP server for execution.
115: 
116: In this mode, **no authentication through this skill is needed**. The skill acts purely as a knowledge layer — the MCP server handles authentication and API execution.
117: 
118: ## Direct Microsoft Graph API Execution
119: 
120: When no Graph MCP server is available, this skill can authenticate to Microsoft 365 and execute Microsoft Graph API calls directly.
121: 
122: ### Authentication
123: 
124: The tool supports **delegated (user)** and **app-only (application)** authentication, auto-detected from environment variables.
125: 
126: **Quick start:**
127: 
128: ```
129: msgraph auth status          # check if signed in
130: msgraph auth signin          # sign in (opens browser) - recommended
131: msgraph auth signin --device-code  # sign in via device code (headless)
132: msgraph auth signout         # clear the session
133: ```
134: 
135: - **Delegated auth** (default): Interactive browser sign-in, with device code fallback for headless environments. Supports incremental consent — on 403, the tool re-authenticates with required scopes and retries automatically.
136: - **App-only auth**: Auto-detected when `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`, `MSGRAPH_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`, or `MSGRAPH_AUTH_METHOD=managed-identity` is set. Requires `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID`.
137: 
138: For detailed authentication configuration including certificates, managed identity, workload identity federation, and all environment variables, see [references/docs/authentication.md](references/docs/authentication.md).
139: 
140: ### Making Graph API Calls
141: 
142: **IMPORTANT**: Run `msgraph auth status` before the first `graph-call` in a session to verify authentication.
143: 
144: ```
145: msgraph graph-call <METHOD> <URL> [flags]
146: ```
147: 
148: #### Read Operations
149: 
150: ```
151: msgraph graph-call GET /me
152: msgraph graph-call GET /users --select "displayName,mail" --top 10
153: msgraph graph-call GET /me/messages --filter "isRead eq false" --top 5 --select "subject,from,receivedDateTime"
154: msgraph graph-call GET /users --filter "startsWith(displayName,'John')"
155: ```
156: 
157: #### Write Operations
158: 
159: **IMPORTANT**: YOU MUST ask the user for confirmation before any write operation. Write operations require the `--allow-writes` flag.
160: 
161: ```
162: msgraph graph-call POST /me/sendMail --body '{"message":{"subject":"Hello","body":{"content":"Hi"},"toRecipients":[{"emailAddress":{"address":"user@example.com"}}]}}' --allow-writes
163: msgraph graph-call PATCH /me --body '{"jobTitle":"Engineer"}' --allow-writes
164: ```
165: 
166: **DELETE is always blocked** regardless of flags.
167: 
168: #### graph-call Flags
169: 
170: | Flag | Description | Example |
171: |---|---|---|
172: | `--select` | OData $select | `--select "displayName,mail"` |
173: | `--filter` | OData $filter | `--filter "isRead eq false"` |
174: | `--top` | OData $top (limit results) | `--top 10` |
175: | `--expand` | OData $expand | `--expand "members"` |
176: | `--orderby` | OData $orderby | `--orderby "displayName desc"` |
177: | `--api-version` | `v1.0` or `beta` (default: beta) | `--api-version v1.0` |
178: | `--scopes` | Request additional permission scopes | `--scopes "Mail.Read"` |
179: | `--headers` | Custom HTTP headers | `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"` |
180: | `--body` | Request body (JSON) | `--body '{"key":"value"}'` |
181: | `--output` | `json` (default) or `raw` | `--output raw` |
182: | `--allow-writes` | Allow POST/PUT/PATCH (requires user confirmation) | |
183: 
184: ## Critical Rules
185: 
186: ### Always (search and knowledge)
187: 
188: 1. **Never guess or fabricate Microsoft Graph endpoints** — always verify via search before calling. This skill exists because agents hallucinate endpoints; use it.
189: 2. **Use the progressive lookup strategy** — start with what you know, then sample-search, api-docs-search, openapi-search as needed.
190: 3. **Use `--select`** to reduce response size — only request fields you need.
191: 4. **Use `--top`** to limit results — avoid fetching thousands of records.
192: 5. **ConsistencyLevel header** is required for `$count` and `$search` on directory objects (users, groups, etc.). Use `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"`.
193: 6. **Default API version is beta** — use `--api-version v1.0` for production-stable endpoints.
194: 
195: ### When using direct execution (graph-call)
196: 
197: 7. **Check auth status** before the first `graph-call` in a session.
198: 8. **GET is the default** — no special flags needed.
199: 9. **Write operations require `--allow-writes`** — YOU MUST confirm with the user first.
200: 10. **DELETE is always blocked** — inform the user this is not supported.
201: 11. **403 triggers automatic re-auth** — the tool requests additional scopes and retries (delegated auth only).
202: 12. **All output is JSON** — parse `statusCode` and `body` fields from the response.
203: 
204: ## Error Handling
205: 
206: | Status | Meaning | Action |
207: |---|---|---|
208: | 401 | Token expired | Run `msgraph auth signin` again |
209: | 403 | Insufficient permissions | Tool auto-retries with incremental consent. If still fails, user needs admin consent. |
210: | 404 | Resource not found | Verify the endpoint path |
211: | 429 | Rate limited | Wait for Retry-After duration, then retry |
212: 
213: ## Environment Variables
214: 
215: | Variable | Description | Default |
216: |---|---|---|
217: | `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID` | Custom Entra ID app client ID | Microsoft Graph CLI Tools app |
218: | `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID` | Target tenant ID (required for app-only) | `common` |
219: | `MSGRAPH_API_VERSION` | Default API version | `beta` |
220: | `MSGRAPH_INDEX_DB_PATH` | Path to OpenAPI index database | Auto-detected |
221: | `MSGRAPH_SAMPLES_DB_PATH` | Path to samples index database | Auto-detected |
222: | `MSGRAPH_API_DOCS_DB_PATH` | Path to API docs index database | Auto-detected |
223: | `MSGRAPH_NO_TOKEN_CACHE` | Disable persistent token cache (in-memory only) | `false` |
224: 
225: For the full list of authentication environment variables, see [references/docs/authentication.md](references/docs/authentication.md).
226: 
227: ## Compatibility
228: 
229: Search tools run fully offline with no network access required. Direct API execution requires network access to `login.microsoftonline.com` and `graph.microsoft.com`. A system browser is used for interactive auth; falls back to device code flow in headless environments.
230: 
231: ## Reference Files
232: 
233: Load these on demand when you need specific guidance. Do NOT load them preemptively.
234:

3: Thank you for your interest in contributing! This document covers how to add community query samples.
4: 
5: ## Why contribute?
6: 
7: Large language models are trained on data that's months old — they don't know about the latest Graph APIs or endpoint changes. Some Graph API docs and endpoints aren't always clear either. Your working query samples go directly into the skill's search index, helping every AI agent using this skill find the right API call.
8: 
9: Read more: [Why Your Samples Matter](https://graph.pm/improve/why-samples-matter/)
10: 
11: ## Query Samples
12: 
13: The skill includes a library of community-contributed query samples that help AI agents find the right Microsoft Graph API call. Each sample maps a natural-language intent to an exact API query.
14: 
15: ### File format
16: 
17: Each sample is a YAML file with two fields:
18: 
19: ```yaml
20: intent: List all Conditional Access policies
21: query: GET /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies
22: ```
23: 
24: For multi-step queries:
25: 
26: ```yaml
27: intent: Get users assigned to the Global Administrator role
28: query:
29:   - GET /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions?$filter=displayName eq 'Global Administrator'
30:   - GET /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments?$filter=roleDefinitionId eq '{id from step 1}'&$expand=principal
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Directory structure
34: 
35: Place your file in the appropriate product directory under `samples/` at the repo root:
36: 
37: ```
38: samples/
39: ├── entra/          # Entra ID (identity, conditional access, roles, apps)
40: ├── exchange/       # Exchange Online (mail, calendar, mailbox)
41: ├── general/        # Cross-product (licensing, organization, domains)
42: ├── intune/         # Intune (device management, compliance, apps)
43: ├── security/       # Microsoft Security (Defender, alerts, hunting)
44: ├── sharepoint/     # SharePoint Online (sites, lists, documents)
45: └── teams/          # Microsoft Teams (teams, channels, messages)
46: ```
47: 
48: ### How to contribute
49: 
50: 1. Fork this repository
51: 2. Create a new `.yaml` file in the appropriate product directory:
52:    ```
53:    samples/{product}/{descriptive-name}.yaml
54:    ```
55: 3. Add your `intent` and `query` fields
56: 4. Submit a pull request
57: 
58: Or use the web form at [graph.pm/improve/add-sample](https://graph.pm/improve/add-sample/) to submit via the browser.
59: 
60: ### Guidelines
61: 
62: - **One sample per file** — eliminates merge conflicts when multiple people contribute
63: - **Use descriptive file names** — `list-conditional-access-policies.yaml`, not `sample1.yaml`
64: - **Be specific in the intent** — "List all Conditional Access policies" beats "Get policies"
65: - **Include the full query path** — `GET /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies`
66: - **Use `$select` where appropriate** — helps agents return only needed fields
67: - **Test your query** — verify it works against the Graph API before submitting
68: 
69: ### When to contribute
70: 
71: If an AI agent struggled to find the right Graph API call and you had to manually construct it, that's the perfect candidate for a new sample.
72: 
73: ### Build & validation
74: 
75: Run the samples index builder locally to validate your contribution:
76: 
77: ```bash
78: make samples
79: ```
80: 
81: This compiles all YAML files into `skills/msgraph/references/samples-index.json`. If your file has syntax errors or is missing required fields, the build will fail with an error message pointing to the problematic file.
82: 
83: You can then test your sample is searchable:
84: 
85: ```bash
86: go run . sample-search --query "your intent keywords"
87: ```
88:

3: This reference covers common Graph API patterns, resources, and conventions that agents should know when constructing API calls.
4: 
5: ## Base URL
6: 
7: ```
8: https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/{resource}
9: ```
10: 
11: - **beta** (default): `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/`
12: - **v1.0** (stable): `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/`

14: ## Common Resources
15: 
16: ### Identity & Directory
17: 
18: | Resource | Path | Common Operations |
19: |---|---|---|
20: | Current user | `/me` | GET profile, PATCH update |
21: | Users | `/users` | GET list, POST create |
22: | Specific user | `/users/{id or UPN}` | GET, PATCH, DELETE |
23: | Groups | `/groups` | GET list, POST create |
24: | Group members | `/groups/{id}/members` | GET list |
25: | Service principals | `/servicePrincipals` | GET list |

27: | Directory roles | `/directoryRoles` | GET list |
28: | Domains | `/domains` | GET list |
29: | Organization | `/organization` | GET details |
30: 
31: ### Mail
32: 
33: | Resource | Path | Common Operations |
34: |---|---|---|
35: | Messages | `/me/messages` | GET list |
36: | Specific message | `/me/messages/{id}` | GET, PATCH, DELETE |
37: | Send mail | `/me/sendMail` | POST |

95: ## OData Query Parameters
96: 
97: ### $select — Choose fields
98: 
99: ```
100: /users?$select=displayName,mail,userPrincipalName
101: ```
102: 
103: ### $filter — Filter results
104: 
105: ```
106: /users?$filter=startsWith(displayName,'John')
107: /users?$filter=department eq 'Engineering'
108: /me/messages?$filter=isRead eq false
109: /users?$filter=accountEnabled eq true
110: ```
111: 
112: ### $top — Limit results
113: 
114: ```
115: /users?$top=10
116: ```
117: 
118: ### $orderby — Sort results
119: 
120: ```
121: /users?$orderby=displayName
122: /me/messages?$orderby=receivedDateTime desc
123: ```
124: 
125: ### $expand — Include related resources
126: 
127: ```
128: /groups/{id}?$expand=members
129: /me/messages/{id}?$expand=attachments
130: ```
131: 
132: ### $count — Get count (requires ConsistencyLevel header)
133: 
134: ```
135: /users/$count
136: ```
137: Use with header: `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`
138: 
139: ### $search — Search (requires ConsistencyLevel header)
140: 
141: ```
142: /users?$search="displayName:John"
143: ```
144: Use with header: `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`
145: 
146: ### Combining parameters
147: 
148: ```
149: /users?$select=displayName,mail&$filter=department eq 'Sales'&$top=25&$orderby=displayName
150: ```
151: 
152: ## Common Permission Scopes
153: 
154: | Scope | Description |
155: |---|---|
156: | `User.Read` | Read current user profile |
157: | `User.Read.All` | Read all user profiles |
158: | `User.ReadWrite.All` | Read and write all user profiles |
159: | `Mail.Read` | Read user mail |
160: | `Mail.ReadWrite` | Read and write user mail |
161: | `Mail.Send` | Send mail as user |
162: | `Calendars.Read` | Read user calendars |
163: | `Calendars.ReadWrite` | Read and write user calendars |
164: | `Group.Read.All` | Read all groups |
165: | `Group.ReadWrite.All` | Read and write all groups |
166: | `Directory.Read.All` | Read directory data |
167: | `Directory.ReadWrite.All` | Read and write directory data |
168: | `Files.Read` | Read user files |
169: | `Files.ReadWrite` | Read and write user files |
170: | `Sites.Read.All` | Read SharePoint sites |
171: | `Sites.ReadWrite.All` | Read and write SharePoint sites |
172: | `Team.ReadBasic.All` | Read basic team info |
173: | `Channel.ReadBasic.All` | Read basic channel info |
174: | `ChannelMessage.Read.All` | Read channel messages |
175: | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | Read managed devices |
176: | `SecurityEvents.Read.All` | Read security events |
177: | `AuditLog.Read.All` | Read audit logs |
178: 
179: ## Pagination
180: 
181: Graph API uses `@odata.nextLink` for pagination:
182: 
183: ```json
184: {
185:   "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/users?$skiptoken=...",
186:   "value": [...]
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: To get the next page, make a GET request to the `@odata.nextLink` URL directly.
191: 
192: ## Batch Requests
193: 
194: Send multiple requests in a single HTTP call:
195: 
196: ```
197: POST /beta/$batch
198: Content-Type: application/json
199: 
200: {
201:   "requests": [
202:     { "id": "1", "method": "GET", "url": "/me" },
203:     { "id": "2", "method": "GET", "url": "/me/messages?$top=5" }
204:   ]
205: }
206: ```
207: 
208: ## Error Response Format
209: 
210: ```json
211: {
212:   "error": {
213:     "code": "Authorization_RequestDenied",
214:     "message": "Insufficient privileges to complete the operation.",
215:     "innerError": {
216:       "date": "2024-01-15T10:00:00",
217:       "request-id": "..."
218:     }
219:   }
220: }
221: ```
222: 
223: ## Tips
224: 
225: 1. **Use $select** to reduce response size — only request fields you need
226: 2. **Use $top** to limit results — avoid fetching thousands of records
227: 3. **Check $filter support** — not all properties support filtering
228: 4. **ConsistencyLevel header** is required for $count and $search on directory objects
229: 5. **User identifier** can be the object ID or userPrincipalName (email)
230: 6. **Group identifier** must be the object ID
